The ADR's §6 seam list is the contract; superseded with the record kept (the supersession comment on PR #1747).
- №1739: the executor's terminal EATS the two-character sequence `[m` — the repo's frozen mock marker is `[mock-llm:<hex>]`, but every DISPLAY of it shows `ock-llm:<hex>]`. The first CI round of this naryad failed precisely on this (assertions written from the display, not the bytes); fixed by a byte-level audit (`od`/python `count(b"[mock-llm")`). The lesson lands in the chain discipline: marker literals are verified at the BYTE level, never by eye.
- №1739: the process-global GLOBAL_SMART_ROUTER persists ACROSS tests within one integration binary — №879's T3 (the empty `llm{}` install) silently re-routed T4's fallback-lane call (the `[MOCK:` pin) through the empty-chain seam. Fixed with the explicit `clear_global_smart_router()` hygiene at the affected seams; the class («router state persists across FILE_LOCK'd tests») applies to every future LLM-surface test that pins the ROUTER-ABSENT lane.
- №1740: the first iteration of this naryad (PR #1748's original head `40f04530`) carried a probe bug its own CI never caught (it was never CI'd): `has_covered_local_fallback` as a bare `any(t == "local")` answers FALSE for the empty roster, while the first iteration's own test asserted the local-first default IS coverage — a red-on-main waiting to happen. The rebuild fixes the probe (`any(..) || is_empty()`) and keeps the mechanics (the local rung + the probe + the keyless anthropic refusal). The lesson: a never-CI'd stack is a liability to supersede, not a reference to trust.
- №1741: the machine source needed a shared-loader extension — `load_floors_strict` (the №846 discipline) refused ANY non-goal_ line, so the registry rows (`check <name> offline=yes|no`) ride the SAME goals file only after the loader learned to skip the declared roster class. The extension is additive (the strictness for goal_ lines unchanged) — a goals file is now a two-class data file (floors + roster), and every future gate that combines both must extend the same way or split its files.
- №1742: the dispatch PROJECTED a drift («новые llm-типы контракта (№879) сдвигают поверхность») — the ride's verified fact is the opposite: the counters are registry-scoped, and a wave that adds no registry rows shifts NOTHING. The ride's product is the verified record itself; the lesson for future dispatches: name the counter's machine source when projecting a drift (the registry, the module tree, or the lock file — each behaves differently).
- №1743: the first CI round of this ride failed on exactly the class the dependabot diff does NOT show: the lock entries moved, but the API break (`column_names(): Vec → Iterator`) lived in the CONSUMER code. A dep-bump ride's review must grep the CONSUMER surface for the bumped crate's API (the changelog of the new version), not just trust the lock diff — the office's dispatch form (№865's «BREAKING → CHANGELOG + upgrade-доки») applies to internal consumers too when the API actually moves.
